tasks.spec:
You are a code worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of freytag-forge; edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. You own ONLY storygame/runtime/reference_resolution.py, the NEW file tests/test_reference_protected.py, and (only to add one small shared predicate) storygame/runtime/knowledge.py. Touch nothing else; never remove or weaken an existing assertion. Never run anything billed or networked.

BACKGROUND. storygame/runtime/reference_resolution.py resolves bare scene-local head nouns before narration (read it fully, plus tests/test_reference_resolution.py, tests/test_reference_clarification.py, tests/test_reference_evidence_append.py). _scene_things() lists every in-scope item/NPC/group; _noun_matches groups them by head noun; two or more things sharing a head produce a fixed clarification question; exactly one is resolved (its full display name is appended to the evidence input via resolved_reference_names; the command text is left as typed - keep that). The owner's required behavior, in his words:
 1. A player refers to an in-scene thing without its adjective ('card' for 'memory card'): no ambiguity, so it resolves automatically to the full thing.
 2. The bare noun fits more than one in-scope thing (Kristin holds a 'transit card' and a 'memory card' is in the scene): the player is asked which one (existing fixed question).
 3. PROTECTED things are out of scope for clarification. If the player says 'card', holds a 'transit card', and the 'memory card' is protected, there is no ambiguity and 'card' resolves to 'transit card'.
Rules 1 and 2 already work. YOUR JOB IS RULE 3.

DEFINITION OF PROTECTED (reuse, do not invent a second notion). A thing is protected when the narration guard would still refuse to let the narrator name it because the knowledge that introduces it has not been earned yet. Read storygame/runtime/narration_safety.py::_validate_segments: `earned_ids` (knowledge entries KnowledgeProjector._established and _visible_to player), `leak_term_to_knowledge`, `entity_alias_to_entities`, `protected_terms`, `disclosure_guards` with unlock_fact / unlock_knowledge_id. Concretely in the Continuity Initiative story: memory_card in scene 1A is protected until knowledge k_sl_1a_b_r0 (leak_terms 'memory card', 'the card', ..., entity_ids includes memory_card, establishes fact memory_card_recovered) is earned; after that it is not protected. Add ONE small function in storygame/runtime/knowledge.py (for example `entity_is_protected(state, entity_id) -> bool`) that answers this from the package indexes and current RuntimeState without calling a model, and use it in _scene_things() so protected things are skipped. Prefer deriving it from the same earned-knowledge calculation the validator uses; if you must duplicate a few lines, say so in your final message. A thing that no knowledge entry or guard mentions is NOT protected. Do not change narration_safety.py.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOR AFTER YOUR CHANGE (all offline, scripted):
 a) 1A before discovery (fresh scene-1A state, k_sl_1a_b_r0 not earned): 'Search the card.' / 'Take the card.' matches no in-scope thing, so resolve_references returns passthrough, no question, no resolutions, and resolved_reference_names is empty (the guard's existing refusal still applies; do not touch it).
 b) 1A after k_sl_1a_b_r0 is earned (memory_card_recovered true, card carried by Kristin): 'Read the card.' resolves uniquely to memory_card; resolved_reference_names returns ('Michelle's memory card' or whatever display_name gives).
 c) Ambiguity: build a state (extend the helper style of tests/test_reference_resolution.py; a tiny synthetic package fixture is fine if the real story cannot express it) with two unprotected cards in scope: 'Use the card.' asks the fixed question listing both names; answering 'transit' splices correctly.
 d) Rule 3: same state but the memory card is protected (its introducing knowledge unearned) and Kristin holds a transit card: 'Use the card.' returns no question and resolves to the transit card.
 e) Protection lifts mid-session: after the earning fact is asserted, case d becomes case c (a question).
 f) Non-card regression: the 2B 'terminal' ambiguity and the 1A-1C 'seat' ambiguity still ask exactly as before.
Write these as tests/test_reference_protected.py. Confirm tests a) and d) fail on the old reference_resolution.py (git stash the source files) and say so in the final message.

ALSO REPORT (do not fix): in your final message, state in plain words what happens end to end for typed 'card' in 1A before discovery and after discovery given the guard as it stands today, and whether the narrator naming bare 'card' for the transit card in case d would still be refused by NarrationSafetyValidator (read the code; run a tiny offline probe through validate() if you can do it without a model). This feeds a later, separate guard decision.

HOW TO RUN. Confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside this worktree. Iterate with `PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --no-cov -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_reference_protected.py tests/test_reference_resolution.py tests/test_reference_clarification.py tests/test_reference_evidence_append.py tests/test_web_demo_clarification.py`, then the whole tests directory, then /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/ruff check and ruff format --check (line length 120) on your files.

COMPLETION RULE: do not stop until the full suite is green and ruff is clean. Finish by listing files changed, pasting the pytest summary, the fail-on-old-code statement, and the end-to-end report.
tasks.verified: protected things are excluded from reference resolution and clarification, so a bare noun resolves to the one unprotected thing
